title: Multi-level Mixture of Experts for Multimodal Entity Linking

problem.claim: Multimodal Entity Linking links ambiguous mentions in multimodal contexts to associated entities in a multimodal knowledge base.

gap.claim: Existing approaches do not address mention ambiguity caused by sparse textual context or dynamic selection of the importance of different modal information.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes a Multi-level Mixture of Experts model for Multimodal Entity Linking.
The model enhances mentions using matching WikiData descriptions and extracts textual and visual embeddings for mentions and entities.
Intra-level and inter-level mixture-of-experts modules dynamically select features from relevant information regions.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments on WikiMEL, RichpediaMEL, and WikiDiverse are reported to demonstrate outstanding performance compared with the state of the art.
The authors report that MMoE code is available online.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work addresses linking ambiguous multimodal mentions to entities in a multimodal knowledge base.
Existing methods use multimodal interaction and fusion for modality bridging and multi-grained semantic matching.
Prior methods leave mention ambiguity and dynamic modal-content selection insufficiently addressed.
MMoE combines description-aware mention enhancement, multimodal feature extraction, and intra-level and inter-level expert selection.
The authors report strong results across three datasets and provide code.

source_observation.claim: The method uses separate expert-selection mechanisms within and across levels to select relevant multimodal features.

interpretation.claim: Hierarchical routing may help adapt feature use when relevance varies across information granularity.

application.claim: For multimodal matching systems, consider routing mechanisms that adapt feature selection at multiple representational levels.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when hierarchical routing is preferable to simpler fusion or routing strategies.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative results or baseline-specific comparisons.
The abstract does not describe dataset sizes, experimental settings, or ablation findings.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported performance.
